questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: After I made the decision to apply for exchange I wanted to go to an English speaking country far away that I yet had not visited and I have always wanted to travel Australia so this was an obvious opportunity.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Studying abroad in Sydney has been one of the greatest experiences of my life. It’s a wonderful country with beautiful nature, vibrant cities, prestigious universities, and a rich culture, among many other things.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The University of Sydney (USYD) and KU were extremely efficient in providing the necessary information, making the process very easy despite the many steps involved, such as visa application, insurance, enrolment applications, and unit selection.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: USYD and the accommodation I stayed in provided excellent information about living in Australia and navigating a foreign university system, making me feel comfortable and well-prepared upon arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are about 4 different possibilities for campus housing and it varies in price and facilities. I chose The Queen Mary Building, which is one of the largest student accommodations in Australia, offering a great opportunity to meet people in similar situations from all over the world.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were no options for meal plans, but the facilities at QMB are decent, with clean kitchens and lots of space.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are plenty of social activities organized by QMB, which was a nice touch. It is quite expensive (around 7800 DKK), but it is possible to find something cheaper if you're willing to put in the effort.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The application process for the accommodation was straightforward, but you need to act quickly to secure a room. The facilities at QMB are decent, with clean kitchens and bathrooms.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration process of enrolment is straightforward but time-consuming.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You will get in touch with a study-abroad adviser from USYD and through email correspondences they will guide you through the different processes of enrolment and time-table management.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You have a study-abroad adviser and you can always contact this person if you have any questions and they reply relatively quick.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the units of study that I applied for and everything was possible in my time-table.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read your email feed carefully and then you will be fine (-;

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They offer some great units of study, but the options for exchange students in life sciences were somewhat limited.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level of the courses are similar to what I’m used to back home in Copenhagen. However, it seems more common not to read at all, as the lecture PowerPoints, workshops, lab sessions, etc., make up the course curriculum. All in all, I found it a bit less challenging, although all four units of study I participated in were within the life sciences field.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is very similar to UCPH in terms of lectures, lab sessions, and workshops. However, the examination system differs from UCPH, as the final exam typically counts for 40-50% of the final grade. You also have midterms, which (at least for my units) accounted for 15-25% of the final grade. This means you should expect smaller quizzes and assignments, each contributing between 3-15% to the final grade. In Australia, multiple-choice questions are very popular, and they were included in all my midterms and final exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BCMB3003 Biochemistry of Human Disease
BCMB3004 Beyond the Genome
BIOS1171 Neuroscience
MIMI2002 Microbes, Infection and Immunity

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
BCMB3004 Beyond the Genome was a great unit where you learn about various methods using mass spectrometry to analyze changes in healthy and diseased cells. The lab component of this unit was very well-structured, and it was interesting to perform different mass spectrometry analyses and gain some experience in bioinformatics. 

Microbes, infection and immunity was also a very well structured unit with a lot of basic learning about the immune respons to pathogens and microbes.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: To get a student visa, you need overseas student health coverage (OSHC), which I didn’t know beforehand (around 1900 DKK). There were also some unforeseen fees for the student accommodation.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general, prices are similar to Copenhagen, but I think groceries and alcohol are more expensive in Sydney.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The University of Sydney Union (USU) offers a wide range of clubs and sports, and it's very affordable (tennis, surf camps, bouldering, dancing), so this opportunity should be exploited. Additionally, they provide pantries (a great opportunity to get free food), cheap coffee, and parties.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recommend the surf-camp (weekend-trip) strongly.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore Sydney in the weekends - go for a hike!!! In the holidays travel Australia (east-coast, Tasmania, Melbourne, New Zealand, Bali?)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to adjust as the culture of Australia is very similar to Europe.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in some of the clubs, go to the parties on campus, talk to your mates in the classes or at your accommodation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Australian people are very kind and polite, so if you're unsure about something, feel free to ask a stranger!!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Remember why you decided to go on exchange and focus on that – what weighs the most, the academic experience or the travel experience?
- Keep up from the start and try not to fall too far behind, because you’ll soon have a quiz or a submission that counts towards your overall grade.
- Enjoy it while it lasts, because it will be over soon!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get new friends from Denmark and all around the world, and to travel one of the most beautiful countries in the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during the exchange was adapting to a different academic system and finding a balance between studying and exploring the new environment. It was a bit overwhelming at first, especially with the different exam formats and the fast pace, but over time, I learned to manage my time better and make the most of the experience both academically and personally.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
